entries.clue: Pressure to replace article in the end? That's as low as it gets (5)

annotation.definition: That's as low as it gets

indicatorNotes.to replace: P takes the place of A, so the new letter sits where the article was

blocks.note: death is the end of life
P is the physics symbol for pressure
A is the indefinite article, and it is the letter swapped out of DEATH

annotation.surface: Someone at their lowest point, asking whether it all ends in death under pressure.
annotation.walkthrough: "In" places the swap inside DEATH; the definition is a whole phrase, since the depth of something is the lowest point it reaches.
annotation.definitionFit: The depth is the deepest point, as low as anything goes.

entries.clue: Fool declines credit (8)

blocks.note: prices that decline dip
tick is British slang for credit, as in buying on tick

annotation.surface: A foolish person turning down an offer of credit.
annotation.walkthrough: "Declines" reads as refuses, but it is the verb dips; buying "on tick" is a British phrase for buying on credit.
annotation.definitionFit: A dipstick is informal slang for a stupid person.

entries.clue: Pond-dwellers came and a pair reproduced (9)

indicatorNotes.reproduced: reproduced means produced again, here in a new arrangement of the letters

blocks.note: CAME + A + PAIR, with "and" joining them

annotation.surface: Some pond creatures turned up in twos and bred.
annotation.walkthrough: Paramecia are single-celled organisms that do reproduce by dividing, so the surface is close to biology.
annotation.definitionFit: Paramecia are freshwater protozoa found in ponds.

entries.clue: Excursion heading off after hot period (4)

indicatorNotes.heading off: the head, or first letter, of TOUR comes off
indicatorNotes.after: after sets order in time or place, so the shortened excursion is placed behind the letter for hot

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
a tour is an excursion; without its first letter it is OUR

annotation.surface: A trip setting off after a spell of hot weather.
annotation.walkthrough: "Hot period" looks like a heatwave, but hot is only the letter H and period is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym at the loose end: sixty minutes is a fixed period, and the word also covers any spell, as in the hour of need.

entries.clue: Distracted cast not currently performing (5,3)

blocks.note: to cast is to throw; past tense threw
an actor who is off is not on stage

annotation.surface: A theatre company in a daze on their night off.
annotation.walkthrough: "Cast" looks like the actors in a play, but it is the verb meaning threw.
annotation.definitionFit: To throw someone off is to distract them or put them off their stride.

entries.clue: Time-study men, I now see, set up record year (8)

indicatorNotes.set up: in a down clue, set up turns the letters so they read upwards

blocks.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
oh is what you say when you suddenly understand
a log is a record, as a ship's log
Y is the abbreviation for year

annotation.surface: Researchers timing workers, suddenly understanding, compile a record for the year.
annotation.walkthrough: "Time-study men" reads as efficiency experts, but the hyphenated phrase ends at study; men starts the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Literal Greek: hora means hour and -logy means study, so the word is built from exactly those two parts.

entries.clue: Key American gym crew with time clocking mechanism (10)

blocks.note: Esc is the escape key on a keyboard
A is the abbreviation for American
PE is physical education, gym at school
a crew is a group of men
T is the abbreviation for time

annotation.surface: A leading American gym team timing its workouts.
annotation.walkthrough: "Clocking" is a playful way of saying belonging to a clock.
annotation.definitionFit: The escapement is the part of a clock that releases its gear train one tick at a time.

entries.clue: Eye doctor scrubbing cover of sealant round windows (5)

indicatorNotes.cover of: the cover of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

blocks.note: an oculist is an eye specialist
the outer letters of sealant, removed from OCULIST

annotation.surface: An optician cleaning off sealant around some windows.
annotation.walkthrough: "Eye" pulls toward the plural of oculus as eyes, but the definition is the architectural sense.
annotation.definitionFit: An oculus is a round window, as at the top of the Pantheon's dome; oculi is the plural.

entries.clue: Article boring distant relative (6)

indicatorNotes.boring: something boring into a word drills inside it

blocks.note: far means distant
THE is the definite article, set inside FAR after FA

annotation.surface: A newspaper piece that bores a remote family member.
annotation.walkthrough: "Boring" reads as dull, but it means drilling through.
annotation.definitionFit: A father is a close relative, though the surface calls him distant.

entries.clue: Piano lacking seventh note given away (5)

indicatorNotes.lacking: the word is lacking, so it loses, the letters named next

blocks.note: granted means given, handed over
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale, removed from GRANTED

annotation.surface: A piano missing a key, so given away.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface puts a piano with a note missing; the seventh note is the sol-fa syllable TE, not a key on the instrument.
annotation.definitionFit: A shortening: the full name of the large concert instrument drops its second word in everyday talk.

entries.clue: Disorganised runners-up withdrawing names one after another (7)

indicatorNotes.Disorganised: disorganised letters are put in a new order
indicatorNotes.withdrawing: RUNNERS-UP withdraws, takes out, the two Ns

blocks.note: the letters of the fodder
N is the abbreviation for name; two names are two Ns, taken out

annotation.surface: A muddled bunch of second-placed finishers pulling their names from a race one by one.
annotation.walkthrough: "One after another" looks like it means in turn, but it is the definition: someone going after another person.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic reading of an ordinary phrase: one who chases is literally one going after another person.

entries.clue: Handled sports equipment - a scam, they say (7)

indicatorNotes.they say: what people say is heard, so the sound counts, not the spelling

blocks.note: a racket is a dishonest scheme, a swindle

annotation.surface: A bat or racquet sold as part of a swindle.
annotation.walkthrough: "Handled" is literal: a racquet has a handle.
annotation.definitionFit: A racquet is sports equipment with a handle, used in tennis or squash.

entries.clue: Reportedly leaves something taken by the patient (4)

indicatorNotes.Reportedly: what is reported is spoken, so the sound counts

blocks.note: thyme is a herb whose leaves are used in cooking

annotation.surface: A patient said to be taking leaves, like a herbal remedy.
annotation.walkthrough: "Patient" suggests a hospital, but it is the adjective: a patient person takes their time.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: a patient person is said to take their time, so it is the thing they take.

entries.clue: England supporter hoping all playing finally contribute (10)

indicatorNotes.finally: take the final letter of contribute

blocks.note: the main letters of the fodder
the last letter of contribute

annotation.surface: An England fan hoping every player finally chips in.
annotation.walkthrough: "England supporter" reads as a football fan, but it means someone fond of England.
annotation.definitionFit: An Anglophile admires England and English things.

entries.clue: Relax fit for semi-formal attire (6,4)

blocks.note: to lounge is to relax
to suit is to fit, as in that suits you

annotation.surface: A dress code: relaxed but still fit for a smart occasion.
annotation.walkthrough: "Fit for" reads as suitable for, but fit is the wordplay and for is the link.
annotation.definitionFit: A lounge suit is a man's business suit, the standard for a semi-formal dress code.

entries.clue: Bird sound from hen dropping large eggs (6)

indicatorNotes.dropping: dropping a letter lets it fall out

blocks.note: a hen clucks
L is the abbreviation for large, dropped from CLUCK
an O looks like an egg, so two eggs are OO

annotation.surface: A hen clucking as she lays big eggs.
annotation.walkthrough: "Bird sound" looks like the definition, but only "Bird" is; the cuckoo does famously lay its eggs in other birds' nests.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the cuckoo is a grey European bird named after its two-note call.

entries.clue: School uniform summer shirt range (5)

blocks.note: a gam is a school of whales
U is uniform in the NATO alphabet
a T-shirt is the summer shirt

annotation.surface: A school's summer uniform comes in a range of shirts.
annotation.walkthrough: "School uniform" is a single idea in the surface, but school is a group of whales and uniform is a letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, from music: the gamut was originally the whole span of notes, hence the full extent of anything.

entries.clue: Personal counsellor, priest that mostly messed up (9)

indicatorNotes.mostly: most of THAT, with its last letter gone

blocks.note: taken as it is
THAT without its last letter

annotation.surface: A personal adviser, a priest who largely made a mess of things.
annotation.walkthrough: A priest who counsels is plausible, which makes the wordplay hide in plain sight.
annotation.definitionFit: A therapist counsels people individually.

entries.clue: Not saying much about old Yorkshireman in the van (3)

indicatorNotes.in the van: the van is the front, as in vanguard, so take the first letter

blocks.note: C is circa, Latin for about
O is the abbreviation for old
the first letter of Yorkshireman

annotation.surface: A quiet old Yorkshireman riding in a van.
annotation.walkthrough: "Van" looks like a vehicle but is the vanguard, the front; Yorkshiremen are stereotyped as taciturn.
annotation.definitionFit: Coy means reticent, unwilling to say much.

entries.clue: Where to find the time and day some Biblical end arrives (8)

annotation.definition: Where to find the time and day

indicatorNotes.some: only some of the letters are used, a run inside the phrase

blocks.note: biblicAL END ARrives, with the C from Biblical

annotation.surface: The day of reckoning, the end of days, finally arriving on schedule.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface sounds apocalyptic, but the answer is inside the words.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: the chart on the wall that sets out every day and date of the year.

entries.clue: I go back and forth, write, and occasionally double up with a hint of mirth (8)

annotation.definitionNote: the clue speaks as the pendulum itself

indicatorNotes.occasionally: taking letters on some occasions, every other one
indicatorNotes.a hint of: a hint is only the first letter

blocks.note: to pen is to write
the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of double up
the first letter of mirth

annotation.surface: A writer pacing, scribbling, and now and then doubled up laughing.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue is written in the first person, so "I" is the answer describing itself.
annotation.definitionFit: A description in the answer's own voice: the weight in a clock swings to and fro.

entries.clue: Trouble with inspiration for Springsteen? Quietly new drug embraced by support group (5)

indicatorNotes.embraced by: the inner letters are hugged by the outer ones

blocks.note: AA is Alcoholics Anonymous
p is piano, quiet in music
N is the abbreviation for new
E is ecstasy

annotation.surface: Bruce Springsteen suffering writer's block, then entering rehab.
annotation.walkthrough: Inspiration here is breathing in; "for Springsteen" flags the American spelling, as British English writes apnoea.
annotation.definitionFit: Apnea is a pause in breathing, literally trouble with breathing in.

entries.clue: Exist as an essential part where the definition ought to be (6)

annotation.definition2: where the definition ought to be

blocks.clueFragment: where the definition ought to be
blocks.note: the definition ought to be inside this very clue, so split the answer into two words

annotation.surface: A self-referential note about where a definition belongs.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half points at the clue itself: the definition ought to be in here.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a formal verb for being intrinsic to something, and, split into two words, a pointer to the clue itself.

entries.clue: The first half of the alphabet at first is centrepiece of elemental building blocks (6)

indicatorNotes.at first: take only the first letter of each of the next two words

blocks.clueFragment: The first half of the alphabet
blocks.note: A to M is the first half of the alphabet
the first letters of is and centrepiece

annotation.surface: An alphabet lesson treating the first thirteen letters as the core building blocks.
annotation.walkthrough: "Centrepiece" looks like a middle-letter instruction, but it only supplies its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Atomic means relating to atoms, the building blocks of the elements.

entries.clue: Exhausted genteel American behind mirror (5)

indicatorNotes.Exhausted: an exhausted word is emptied, leaving only its outer letters

blocks.note: genteel emptied of its middle
ass is American slang for the backside

annotation.surface: A tired, refined American admiring their rear in the mirror.
annotation.walkthrough: "Exhausted" reads as tired, but it empties genteel; "behind" reads as position, but it is the noun.
annotation.definitionFit: A shortening of looking glass, the old word for a mirror.

entries.clue: Craft moral principles leader ditched for commercial treaties (5,5)

indicatorNotes.leader ditched: the leader, the first letter, is thrown away

blocks.note: a craft is a skilled trade
ideals are moral principles; without the I it is DEALS

annotation.surface: A politician abandoning principles to secure trade agreements.
annotation.walkthrough: "Leader" suggests a political leader, but it is only the first letter of ideals.
annotation.definitionFit: Trade deals are commercial agreements between countries.

entries.clue: Panic contained by Territorial Army (5)

indicatorNotes.contained by: the answer is contained inside the next words

blocks.note: territoriAL ARMy

annotation.surface: Fear being kept under control by reserve soldiers.
annotation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army is Britain's volunteer reserve force.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both nouns name a sudden fright.

entries.clue: Palm and what's attached, a bunch of bananas (4)

blocks.note: the palm plus the fingers and thumb joined to it
the growers' word for one cluster cut from the stalk

annotation.surface: Holding a bunch of bananas in the palm.
annotation.walkthrough: The banana sense comes from the fruits' resemblance to fingers; each banana in the cluster is called a finger.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the body part described piece by piece, and a trade term for a cluster of bananas.

entries.clue: Briefly join detachment (4)

indicatorNotes.Briefly: a brief word is cut short, losing its last letter

blocks.note: to unite is to join; it loses its final E

annotation.surface: Signing up to a detachment for a short stint.
annotation.walkthrough: Join and detachment look like opposites, which hides that detachment is a military group.
annotation.definitionFit: A detachment is a military unit sent off on a separate task.

entries.clue: Spoke like a Persian perhaps, but extremely misinformed about every vowel (7)

indicatorNotes.extremely: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters
indicatorNotes.about: M and D go about, around, the vowels

blocks.note: the first and last letters of misinformed
all five vowels, in the order the answer needs

annotation.surface: An Iranian speaking but getting every vowel wrong.
annotation.walkthrough: "Persian" looks like a person from Iran, but it is a Persian cat; the clue does not fix the order of the vowels.
annotation.definitionFit: Miaowed, or miaoued, is the sound a cat makes, so a Persian cat speaks by miaouing.

entries.clue: Unreliable time indicator united island in revolt (7)

indicatorNotes.in revolt: letters in revolt overturn their order

blocks.note: U is the abbreviation for united
taken as it is

annotation.surface: A united island rising up against its rulers.
annotation.walkthrough: A sundial is unreliable because it only works when the sun shines.
annotation.definitionFit: A sundial tells the time, but not on cloudy days or at night.

entries.clue: I'm kept nearby at regular intervals to follow church burial plot (8)

indicatorNotes.at regular intervals: things placed at regular intervals are evenly spaced, so the letters are picked out with equal gaps, every second one
indicatorNotes.to follow: to follow is to come behind, so these letters are placed after the church abbreviation

blocks.note: CE is the Church of England
the even letters of i'M kEpT nEaRbY

annotation.surface: A person kept close to a church, which suits a graveyard.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface's "I'm kept nearby" sounds like a speaker, but those words are just letters to thin out.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a plot here is a piece of ground, and the answer is ground set aside for graves.

entries.clue: Add space symbol (5)

blocks.note: to tot up is to add
an em is a printing space the width of an M

annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an emblem, originally a natural object adopted as the sign of a clan.
annotation.walkthrough: "Add space" sounds like a typing instruction; an em is a typesetter's unit of space.
